exact_statement: Conventional machine-learning intrusion-detection benchmarks provide useful controlled comparisons, but their discrimination metrics do not alone establish validity across chronology, operating points, datasets, prevalence, computational paths, or attack families withheld from development. We conducted a bounded, source-faithful empirical validity audit centered on CSE-CIC-IDS2018, with a restricted CICIDS2017 bridge. The audit separated processed-reference evaluation from source-faithful temporal and transfer populations and examined frozen operating-point transfer, registered feature and explanation sensitivity, direction-specific semantic bridges, analytic prevalence and workload projections, component-level computational profiling, eligible leave-one-attack-family-out evaluation, and finite-seed stability. On the processed reference holdout, balanced XGBoost achieved F1 0.9285 and PR-AUC 0.9776. On one shared forward target, chronological-natural development produced mean PR-AUC 0.6388 versus 0.2599 after random-natural development across five registered realizations; the ordering was descriptive and held in all five, while frozen thresholds transferred poorly. Bridge62 transfer was directional: PR-AUC was 0.667483 from IDS2018 to CICIDS2017 and 0.108176 in the reverse direction. Under an analytic 0.1\% prevalence scenario, projected PPV and analyst workload diverged, including PPV 0.965572 with 33.5 analyst-hours per day for one point. Eligible-family behavior was selective, and computational feasibility was specific to measured compatible paths and hardware. These findings show that IDS conclusions depend on population, protocol, representation, operating rule, and evidence status; they do not establish universal deployment readiness, zero-day detection, temporal causation, or complete historical reproduction.

exact_statement: Machine-learning intrusion-detection benchmarks provide useful controlled evidence. A fixed population, representation, learner, and decision rule can support reproducible comparison of discrimination and operating behavior. Such evidence should not be discarded because it is conditional. It answers a narrower question: how well does a fitted detector separate the labels in the evaluated benchmark under the declared protocol? Network intrusion detection, however, is applied to traffic whose chronology, collection environment, feature contract, prevalence, attack composition, and computational path may differ from those conditions \cite{sommer2010closed,ring2019survey,arp2022dos}.

exact_statement: Consequently, strong benchmark discrimination does not by itself establish future-facing reliability. Ranking metrics describe score ordering, whereas a deployed decision rule depends on a threshold, calibration, prevalence, and action cost \cite{saito2015precision,axelsson2000baserate}.
